<reason>Side A (CON) won by establishing that formal collective bargaining faces decisive legal barriers at public universities in states banning public-sector bargaining—an objection Side B could not neutralize without conceding the motion requires prior legislative reform. A also provided a sharper economic analysis of union incentives and roster costs, distinguishing internal revenue sharing from external NIL to undermine B's cross-subsidization defense.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2 (A1/A2) decisively separated direct revenue sharing from unionization regarding roster elimination, and distinguished external booster NIL from internal university budgets to demonstrate that Title IX compliance protects cross-subsidization in ways union contracts would not.</best_rebuttal>
